summary: EarthLens is an interactive environmental analysis platform built to help researchers, students, policymakers, and climate analysts study real-time changes in temperature, rainfall, humidity, and wind across the globe. Drawing on live, updatable NASA datasets (GISTEMP and POWER), it visualizes environmental shifts through interactive maps, time-series charts, and regional comparisons while applying statistical trend analysis to measure the exact direction, rate, and significance of each change. Users can dynamically refresh NASA feeds, add custom study locations, and export evidence-backed findings to make informed climate decisions.
details:
EarthLens Observatory is an interactive, browser-based climate analysis platform that turns live NASA Earth observation data into clear, statistically verified insights. Designed for researchers, students, policymakers, and analysts, it removes the technical barriers of raw meteorological data so anyone can explore how our planet is changing.

Core Capabilities:

-> Live, Updatable NASA Data: Connects directly to NASA GISTEMP v4 (global/zonal temperature anomalies) and NASA POWER (regional temperature, rainfall, humidity, and wind records). Users can explore 16 pre-loaded global ecosystems—from the Arctic and Amazon to Dhaka and California—or dynamically refresh feeds and add custom locations on demand.

-> Multi-Dimensional Visualization: Combines an interactive global map, time-series charts, and side-by-side regional comparisons so users can instantly pinpoint where anomalies occur and how different regions respond to climate drivers.

-> Built-In Statistical Rigor: Goes beyond visual charts by calculating the exact direction and rate of change alongside statistical significance testing under selectable methods—separating genuine climate trends from natural year-to-year noise.

-> Custom Workspaces & Exports: Allows users to build custom regional studies, pull fresh NASA observations, and export clean data and statistical summaries for research, education, or local planning.

Technical Stack:

-> Built with Next.js, React, and TypeScript with dedicated NASA API proxy routes (/api/nasa/gistemp, /api/nasa/power), styled with Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui, backed by Python/Node.js data validation scripts, and deployed globally on Cloudflare Workers.

Why It Matters:

EarthLens directly answers the NASA Space Apps Challenge by giving users clear, evidence-backed answers to four critical questions: what is changing, where it is happening, by how much, and how strongly the data proves it.
